title: Bekhorot 45
description: The last blemishes of the legs, feet and hands of a priest, the extra finger and its ritual impurity, the count of 248 limbs, Rabbi Tarfon and the man with twenty-four digits, the ambidextrous priest, conditions that disqualify a person but not an animal and the reverse, and the priest who must vow away a forbidden marriage.
topics: 🦶 The last foot blemishes: the ikkel, the protuberance, the heel and the goose-like foot
✋ Joined fingers, and an extra finger with a bone
🔢 An extra digit on a corpse: impure by contact and carrying, but in a tent only if it is counted with the others
🦴 A majority of 248: 125 bones, whether the body has 200 or 281
📖 “Six and six, twenty-four in number”: praise or disgrace? Rabbi Tarfon and the man with extra digits
🎨 Very dark, very red, very white, very tall: what disqualifies a priest but not an animal
🍷 The drunk priest, and Rabbi Yehuda on figs of Ke’ila, milk and honey
💍 The priest who married a forbidden woman: he vows, serves and divorces

a1.he: וּבַעַל הַפִּיקִים, הָעִיקֵּל. אֵיזֶהוּ הָעִיקֵּל? כׇּל שֶׁהוּא מַקִּיף פַּרְסוֹתָיו וְאֵין אַרְכֻּבּוֹתָיו נוֹקְשׁוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ. פִּיקָּה יוֹצֵא מִגּוּדָּלוֹ, עֲקֵיבוֹ יוֹצֵא לַאֲחוֹרָיו, פַּרְסוֹתָיו רְחָבוֹת כְּשֶׁל אַוָּוז.

a2.he: אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו מוּרְכָּבוֹת זוֹ עַל זוֹ, אוֹ קְלוּטוֹת לְמַעְלָה עַד הַפֶּרֶק — כָּשֵׁר, לְמַטָּה מִן הַפֶּרֶק וַחֲתָכָהּ — כָּשֵׁר, הָיְתָה בָּהּ יְתֶרֶת וַחֲתָכָהּ, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ עֶצֶם — פָּסוּל, וְאִם לָאו — כָּשֵׁר.

a3.he: יָתֵר בְּיָדָיו וּבְרַגְלָיו, שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ — עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין. הַשּׁוֹלֵט בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו — רַבִּי פּוֹסֵל וַחֲכָמִים מַכְשִׁירִין.

a4.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶר רֶגֶל, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת הַקִּישָׁן וְהָעִיקֵּל וְהַקִּילְבָּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אוֹ שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל״. תָּנָא: בַּעַל הַקִּיפִּין וְהַשּׁוּפְנָר. אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּעַל הַפִּיקִּין — שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כְּסָתוֹת הַרְבֵּה, שׁוּפְנָר — שֶׁאֵין לוֹ כְּסָתוֹת כׇּל עִיקָּר.

a5.he: פִּיקָּה יוֹצָא מִגּוּדָּלוֹ, וַעֲקֵיבוֹ יוֹצֵא לַאֲחוֹרָיו. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שׁוֹקוֹ יוֹצֵא בָּאֶמְצַע רַגְלוֹ. פַּרְסוֹתָיו רְחָבוֹת כְּשֶׁל אַוָּוז. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא דִּטְרִיפָה וְלָא סְדִיקָא, אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דִּטְרִיפָה, אַף עַל גַּב דִּסְדִיקָא.

a6.he: אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו מוּרְכָּבוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ, אוֹ קְלוּטוֹת. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״שֶׁבֶר יָד״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶר יָד.

a7.he: אֶצְבָּעוֹת מוּרְכָּבוֹת לְמַעְלָה אוֹ קְלוּטוֹת לְמַעְלָה מִן הַפֶּרֶק, וְהָאָמְרַתְּ כָּשֵׁר! אֶלָּא וְלֹא חֲתָכָן, מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אוֹ שֶׁבֶר יָד״.

a8.he: הָיְתָה בּוֹ יְתֶרֶת וַחֲתָכָהּ, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ עֶצֶם — פָּסוּל, וְאִם לָאו — כָּשֵׁר. אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְהוּא שֶׁנִּסְפֶּרֶת עַל גַּבֵּי הַיָּד.

a9.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יְתֵירָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ עֶצֶם, וְאֵין בָּהּ צִפּוֹרֶן — מְטַמָּא בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא, וּמְטַמָּא בְּאֹהֶל, וְעוֹלָה לְמִנְיַן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה. אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּבְנִסְפֶּרֶת עַל גַּב הַיָּד.

a10.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דָּבָר זֶה רַבֵּינוּ הַגָּדוֹל אֲמָרוֹ, הַמָּקוֹם יִהְיֶה בְּעֶזְרוֹ: יְתֶרֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ עֶצֶם וְאֵין בָּהּ צִפּוֹרֶן — מְטַמָּא בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא, וְאֵין מְטַמָּא בְּאֹהֶל. אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּבְשֶׁאֵינָהּ נִסְפֶּרֶת עַל גַּב הַיָּד.

a11.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עָשׂוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם כְּדִבְרֵי נְבִיאוּת, מָה נַפְשָׁךְ? אִי אֵבֶר הוּא — בְּאֹהֶל נָמֵי תְּטַמֵּא, וְאִי לָאו אֵבֶר הוּא — בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא נָמֵי לָא לִיטַמֵּי!

a12.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: מִשּׁוּם עֶצֶם כִּשְׂעוֹרָה נָגְעוּ בָּהּ.

a13.he: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ נִסְפֶּרֶת, אַטּוּ נִסְפֶּרֶת. אִי הָכִי, שֶׁאֵינָהּ נִסְפֶּרֶת בְּאֹהֶל נָמֵי תְּטַמֵּא!

a14.he: עֲבַדוּ רַבָּנַן הֶיכֵּירָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לִישְׂרְפוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ תְּרוּמָה וְקָדָשִׁים.

a15.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: רוֹב בִּנְיָנוֹ וְרוֹב מִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל מֵת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוֹבַע — טְמֵאִין. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ רוֹב בִּנְיָנוֹ? שְׁנֵי שׁוֹקַיִים וְיָרֵךְ אֶחָד, הוֹאִיל וְרוֹב גּוֹבְהוֹ בְּגָדוֹל. אֵיזֶהוּ רוֹב מִנְיָנוֹ? מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה.

a16.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרָבָא: תַּנָּא מִנְיָינָא אֲתָא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן? קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כִּדְתַנְיָא: חָסֵר, שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אֶלָּא מָאתַיִם, וְיָתֵר, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מָאתַיִם וּשְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד — כּוּלָּן עוֹלִין לְמִנְיַן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה, זִיל בָּתַר רוּבָּא דְאִינָשֵׁי.

a17.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִידָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁשָּׁלְקוּ זוֹנָה אַחַת שֶׁנִּתְחַיְּיבָה שְׂרֵיפָה לַמֶּלֶךְ, בָּדְקוּ וּמָצְאוּ בָּהּ מָאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים וּשְׁנַיִם, אָמַר לָהֶם: שֶׁמָּא בְּאִשָּׁה בְּדַקְתֶּם, שֶׁהוֹסִיף לָהּ הַכָּתוּב שְׁנֵי צִירִים וּשְׁנֵי דְּלָתוֹת.

a18.he: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁצִּירִים לַבַּיִת — כָּךְ צִירִים לָאִשָּׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַתִּכְרַע וַתֵּלֶד כִּי נֶהֶפְכוּ עָלֶיהָ צִרֶיהָ״. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁדְּלָתוֹת לַבַּיִת — כָּךְ דְּלָתוֹת לָאִשָּׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי לֹא סָגַר דַּלְתֵי בִטְנִי״.

a19.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמַּפְתֵּחַ לַבַּיִת, כָּךְ מַפְתֵּחַ לָאִשָּׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּפְתַּח אֶת רַחְמָהּ״. לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קַשְׁיָא דְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל! דִּלְמָא אַיְּידֵי דְּזוּטַר אִתְּמוֹחֵי מִתְּמַח.

a20.he: אָמַר רַב: וְכוּלָּן אֵין מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל״, דָּבָר הַשָּׁוֶה לְכׇל אָדָם.

a21.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּבְאִישׁ לֵיכָּא? וְהָכְתִיב: ״צִירִים אֲחָזוּנִי כְּצִירֵי יוֹלֵדָה״! צִירֵי בָשָׂר. וְהָכְתִיב: ״אֲדֹנִי בַּמַּרְאָה נֶהֶפְכוּ צִירַי״! הָכָא נָמֵי צִירֵי בָשָׂר. הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, מָאתַיִם וְאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנֶה הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? לָא בְּאִישׁ וְלָא בְּאִשָּׁה.

b1.he: יָתֵר בְּיָדָיו וּבְרַגְלָיו. אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ, וַתְּהִי עוֹד מִלְחָמָה, וּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי אִישׁ מָדוֹן אֶצְבַּע יָדָיו וְאֶצְבַּע רַגְלָיו שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ״, מָר סָבַר בִּגְנוּתֵיהּ מִשְׁתַּעֵי, וּמָר סָבַר בִּשְׁבָחֵיהּ מִשְׁתַּעֵי.

b2.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: מָה לִי דִּכְתִיב ״שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע מִסְפָּר״? צְרִיכִי, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: שֵׁית דִּידֵיהּ וְשֵׁית דְּכַרְעֵיהּ, כְּתַב ״עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע״. וְאִי כְּתַב ״עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: הוּא חֲמֵשׁ מֵהַאי גִּיסָא וּשְׁבַע מֵהַאי גִּיסָא, כְּתַב ״שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ״. ״מִסְפָּר״ — בְּנִסְפֶּרֶת עַל גַּבֵּי הַיָּד.

b3.he: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, יָתֵר בְּיָדָיו וּבְרַגְלָיו שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע. אָמַר לוֹ: כְּמוֹתְךָ יִרְבּוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל! אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה? כָּךְ אָמַר לוֹ: כְּמוֹתְךָ יִתְמַעֲטוּ מַמְזֵירֵי וּנְתִינֵי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל!

b4.he: הַשּׁוֹלֵט בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן — אִיטֵּר, בֵּין בַּיָּד בֵּין בָּרֶגֶל — פָּסוּל. הַשּׁוֹלֵט בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו — רַבִּי פּוֹסֵל וַחֲכָמִים מַכְשִׁירִין. מָר סָבַר — כְּחִישׁוּתָא אַתְחִלָא בְּיָמִין, וּמָר סָבַר — בְּרִיּוּתָא אַתְחִלָא בִּשְׂמֹאל.

b5.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַכּוּשִׁי, הַגִּיחוֹר, וְהַלַּבְקָן, וְהַקִּפֵּחַ, וְהַנַּנָּס, וְהַחֵרֵשׁ, וְהַשּׁוֹטֶה, וְהַשִּׁיכּוֹר, וּבַעֲלֵי נְגָעִים טְהוֹרִים — פְּסוּלִין בְּאָדָם וּכְשֵׁרִים בַּבְּהֵמָה. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹטָה מִן הַבְּהֵמָה אֵינָהּ מִן הַמּוּבְחָר. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף בַּעֲלֵי הַדִּלְדּוּלִין פְּסוּלִין בָּאָדָם וּכְשֵׁרִין בַּבְּהֵמָה.

b6.he: גְּמָ׳ כּוּשִׁי — אוּכָּמָא, גִּיחוֹר — חִיוָּורָא, לַבְקָן — סוּמָּקָא. אִינִי? וְהָא הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ ״מַאן בָּעֵי לוּקְיָאנֵי״, וְאִישְׁתְּכַח חִיוָּורָא! אֶלָּא: כּוּשִׁי — אוּכָּמָא, גִּיחוֹר — סוּמָּקָא, כִּדְאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי: ״סוּמָּקָא גִּיחְיָא״, לַבְקָן — חִיוָּורָא, כְּהָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ ״מַאן בָּעֵי לוּקְיָאנֵי״, וְאִישְׁתְּכַח חִיוָּורֵי.

b7.he: קִפֵּחַ. תָּנֵי רַב זְבִיד: גָּבוֹהַּ. אִינִי? וְהָתָנֵי רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִשְׁתַּבֵּחַ בְּבַעֲלֵי קוֹמָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאָנֹכִי הִשְׁמַדְתִּי אֶת הָאֱמֹרִי מִפְּנֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר כְּגֹבַהּ אֲרָזִים גׇּבְהוֹ״. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בַּאֲרִיכָא שְׁמִיטָה סַנְיָא.

b8.he: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: גָּבוֹהַּ לֹא יִשָּׂא גְּבוֹהִית — שֶׁמָּא יֵצֵא מֵהֶן תּוֹרֶן, נַנָּס לֹא יִשָּׂא נַנֶּסֶת — שֶׁמָּא יֵצֵא מֵהֶם אֶצְבָּעִי, לָבָן לֹא יִשָּׂא לְבָנָה — שֶׁמָּא יֵצֵא מֵהֶם בּוֹהֵק, שָׁחוֹר לֹא יִשָּׂא שְׁחוֹרָה — שֶׁמָּא יֵצֵא מֵהֶן טָפוּחַ.

b9.he: הַחֵרֵשׁ, הַשּׁוֹטֶה, וְהַשִּׁכּוֹר. שִׁכּוֹר מַחֵיל עֲבוֹדָה, בַּהֲדֵי מוּמֵי דְּמַחֲילִי עֲבוֹדָה בָּעֵי לְמִיחְשַׁב!

b10.he: בִּשְׁאָר דְּבָרִים הַמְשַׁכְּרִים. וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּתַנְיָא: אָכַל דְּבֵילָה קְעִילִית, וְשָׁתָה חָלָב אוֹ דְּבַשׁ, נִכְנַס לַמִּקְדָּשׁ — חַיָּיב.

b11.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵלּוּ כְּשֵׁרִין בָּאָדָם וּפְסוּלִין בַּבְּהֵמָה: אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ, טְרֵיפָה, וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, וְשֶׁנֶּעֶבְדָה בָּהֶן עֲבֵירָה, וְשֶׁהֵמִית אֶת הָאָדָם.

b12.he: וְהַנּוֹשֵׂא נָשִׁים בַּעֲבֵירָה — פָּסוּל עַד שֶׁיַּדִּירֶנָּה הֲנָאָה, וְהַמִּטַּמֵּא לְמֵתִים — פָּסוּל עַד שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא מִטַּמֵּא לְמֵתִים.

b13.he: גְּמָ׳ וְאֵלּוּ כְּשֵׁירִין בָּאָדָם, מַאי (באותו) [״אוֹתוֹ] וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״?

b14.he: אִילֵּימָא אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו, דִּכְוָתֵיהּ תַּיִישׁ וּבְנוֹ, מִי נָהֵיג? וְהָתַנְיָא: ״אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״ נוֹהֵג בִּנְקֵבוֹת, וְאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בִּזְכָרִים! אֶלָּא תְּיָישָׁה וּבְנָהּ, דִּכְוָותַהּ הָכָא כֹּהֶנֶת וּבְנָהּ, כֹּהֶנֶת בַּת עֲבוֹדָה הִיא?

b15.he: לְעוֹלָם אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו, דִּכְוָותַהּ הָכָא תַּיִישׁ וּבְנוֹ. אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין: עֲדָא אָמְרָה חֲנַנְיָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: ״אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״ נוֹהֵג בִּנְקֵבוֹת וְאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בִּזְכָרִים, חֲנַנְיָה אוֹמֵר: נוֹהֵג בִּזְכָרִים וּבִנְקֵבוֹת.

b16.he: וְהַנּוֹשֵׂא נָשִׁים כּוּ׳. תָּנָא: נוֹדֵר וְעוֹבֵד, יוֹרֵד וּמְגָרֵשׁ.

b17.he: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא אָזֵיל לְגַבֵּי חָכָם וְשָׁרֵי לֵיהּ! קָסָבַר: צָרִיךְ לְפָרֵט אֶת הַנֶּדֶר.

b18.he: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר צָרִיךְ לְפָרֵט אֶת הַנֶּדֶר, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין צָרִיךְ לְפָרֵט אֶת הַנֶּדֶר, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר? דְּמַדְּרִינַן לֵיהּ בְּרַבִּים.

b19.he: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בְּרַבִּים אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר? דְּמַדְּרִינַן

messages.text: Continued from 44b: the mishna is listing blemishes of the legs and feet that disqualify a priest, beginning with one whose ankles or knees knock together as he walks.
Mishna
and a ba’al happikim, and the ikkel. What is the ikkel? It is anyone who places his feet together and his knees do not knock into each other, i.e., he is bowlegged.

notes.he: כדמפרש וקמפרש עיקל ברישא כל שהוא מקיף פרסותיו כשיושב ומחבר פרסות רגליו זו לזו ואין ארכובותיו נוקשות זו לזו שעוקמות כלפי חוץ:
notes.en: The ba’al happikin and the ikkel: as [the mishna] explains, and it explains the ikkel first. Anyone who “surrounds his soles”: when he sits and brings the soles of his feet together, his knees do not knock against each other, since they bend outward.

notes.he: שפרסות רגליו רחבות ועגולות שכשהוא מקרב רגליו זו אצל זו אין יכולות ארכובותיו להקיש זו בזו:
notes.en: Anyone who surrounds his soles: his soles are wide and round, so that when he brings his feet close together, his knees cannot knock against each other.

messages.text: A priest with a protuberance emerging alongside the thumb of his hand or the big toe of his foot, or one whose heel emerges and protrudes back from his foot,

notes.he: חתיכת בשר עגול כפיקה יוצאה מגודלו:
notes.en: A protuberance emerging from his thumb: a round piece of flesh, like a knob [pika], protruding from his thumb.

notes.he: כדמפרש בגמרא ששוקו עומד באמצע רגלו שחצי הרגל עומד בפנים וחצי לאחור:
notes.en: His heel emerges behind him: as the Gemara explains, his shin stands in the middle of his foot, so that half the foot is in front and half behind.

notes.he: כעין אצבע יתירה:
notes.en: A protuberance emerging from his thumbs: like an extra finger.

notes.he: שבולט הרבה לאחריו כדמפרש בגמרא כגון שנראה (כגון) שוקו יוצא באמצע רגלו:
notes.en: His heel emerges behind him: it protrudes far behind him, as the Gemara explains: for example, his shin seems to come out of the middle of his foot.

messages.text: or one whose feet are wide like those of a goose are all disqualified from performing the Temple service.

notes.he: שקלושות הן כשל אווז ואין ארכן יתר על רחבן:
notes.en: Wide like a goose’s: they are flat like a goose’s, and their length is no greater than their width.

messages.text: A priest whose fingers or toes are configured one upon the other, or one whose fingers or toes are attached, is likewise disqualified. But if they were attached from above the palm of the hand or the bottom of the foot only until the middle joint, he is fit. If they were attached below the joint, higher up on the finger or toe, and he cut to separate them, he is fit.

notes.he: פרק האמצעי:
notes.en: Until the joint: the middle joint.

notes.he: דהיינו לצד הצפורן שמחוברין כולן וחתכה שיהו מסולקים כשר:
notes.en: Below the joint: that is, toward the nail, where they are all joined; and he cut it so that they are separated: he is fit.

messages.text: In a case where there was an extra finger or toe on his hand or foot and he cut it, if that extra appendage contains a bone, the priest is disqualified even after it was cut, and if there is no bone the priest is fit.

notes.he: אצבע יתירה:
notes.en: Extra: an extra finger.

notes.he: הואיל וחתכה שהרי הוא מחוסר אבר שנמצא בו ואם לאו כשר דלא חשיב אלא תלתול בעלמא:
notes.en: If it contains a bone, he is disqualified: since he cut it off, he is now missing a limb that he had. And if not, he is fit, since it counts as no more than a wart.

messages.text: If there was an extra appendage on his hands and on his feet, six on each for a total of twenty-four, Rabbi Yehuda deems the priest fit and the Rabbis deem him disqualified.

notes.he: מפרש לגבי קרא בגמרא אמאי נקט להו ומתני' לישנא דקרא נקט:
notes.en: Six and six, twenty-four: the Gemara explains, in connection with the verse, why it uses these terms; the mishna simply uses the verse’s wording.

messages.text: With regard to one who is ambidextrous and has control of both of his hands, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi deems the priest disqualified, as his halakhic status is like that of one who is left-handed, and the Rabbis deem him fit.
Gemara
The Sages taught in a baraita:

From the verse that states: “Broken-footed” (Leviticus 21:19), I have derived only that a broken leg disqualifies a priest from performing the Temple service. From where do I derive to include that the kishan, i.e., one who knocks his ankles or his knees together; the ikkel; and the kilvan are disqualified as well? The same verse states: “Or broken-footed.” The term “or” serves to include all blemishes of the leg.

verse.he: אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיֶה בוֹ שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל אוֹ שֶׁבֶר יָד׃
verse.en: no man who has a broken leg or a broken arm;

notes.he: היינו המקיש בקרסוליו:
notes.en: Gemara. The kishan: that is, one who knocks his ankles together.

notes.he: היינו פיקה יוצאה מגודלו:
notes.en: And the ikkel and the kilban: that is, a protuberance emerging from his thumb.

notes.he: לא איתפרש לן [יש מפרשים קילבן שזורק רגלו לאחוריו כשהוא הולך]:
notes.en: And the kilban: it has not been explained to us. [Some explain the kilban as one who throws his leg backward when he walks.]

messages.text: A ba’al hakippin and the shufnar are blemished.

notes.he: בעל הפיקין והשופנר גרסי':
notes.en: We read: ba’al happikin and the shufnar. [Rashi reads happikin, with a pe, where the translation has hakkippin.]

messages.text: A ba’al happikin is one who has large protuberances on his leg, while a shufnar is one who has no protuberances at all.

notes.he: שאיסתמרא שלו שקורין קביל"א גדולה מאד:
notes.en: Many pads [kesatot harbeh]: his ankle bone, which is called (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), is very large. [The translation renders kesatot as “protuberances.”]

notes.dh: בעל הפיקין שיש לו כסתות הרבה
notes.he: פי' בקונט' שאיסתוורא שלו שקורין קביל"א גדולה ובערוך פירש שפרסתו גבוהה ויש בשר הרבה לצד ראש הרגל ובעקב ואמצעית שלו כמין כיפה ולשון כסתות משמע כפירושו דאיירי בבשר ולא בעצם כי ההיא דבראשית רבה דקאמר על האדם המכוסה בית הריעי שלו בעגבותא לו כסתות משא"כ לבהמה:
notes.en: A ba’al happikin, who has many pads [kesatot]: the Kuntres [Rashi] explained that his ankle bone, called (Tosafot repeat Rashi’s Old French gloss), is large. The Arukh explained that his foot is high, with much flesh toward the front of the foot and at the heel, and its middle is like a dome. The word kesatot [cushions] suggests the Arukh’s interpretation, that it speaks of flesh and not of bone, like the passage in Bereshit Rabba that says of a person, whose excretory place is covered by the buttocks, that he has kesatot, which is not so for an animal.

notes.he: כסתות הרבה כעין קרסוליו הרבה:
notes.en: Happikin and the shufnar: many pads, like many ankles.

messages.text: The description: One whose heel emerges and protrudes back from his foot, means his calf, i.e., his lower leg, emerges from the middle of his foot.
messages.quote: a protuberance emerging alongside the thumb of his hand … whose heel emerges and protrudes back from his foot

messages.text: Do not say that this is referring only to one whose feet are entirely like those of a goose, i.e., his feet are flat and his toes are not split. Rather, once one’s feet are flat he is considered blemished, even though his toes are split.
messages.quote: whose feet are wide like those of a goose

notes.he: קלושטנב"א:
notes.en: Tereifa [rendered “flat” in the translation]: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: שדקה הרבה ולא סדיקה בין האצבעות אלא שעגולה כשל אווז אלא כיון דטריפה אע"ג דסדיקה פסול:
notes.en: Do not say flat: very thin, and not split between the toes but round like a goose’s; rather, once it is flat, even if it is split, he is disqualified.

messages.text: The Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: whose fingers or toes are configured one upon the other, or one whose fingers or toes are attached

notes.he: אם דבוקות הן האצבעות מפיסת יד ועד הפרק האמצעי של אצבעות כשר ואם דבוקה למטה מן הפרק וחתך הדבק כשר:
notes.en: Attached until the joint: if the fingers are attached from the palm up to the middle joint of the fingers, he is fit; and if attached below the joint and he cut the attachment, he is fit.

messages.text: The verse states: “Broken-handed” (Leviticus 21:19). I have derived only that a broken hand disqualifies a priest.

verse.he: אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיֶה בוֹ שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל אוֹ שֶׁבֶר יָד׃
verse.en: no man who has a broken leg or a broken arm;

messages.text: From where do I derive that if his fingers or toes are configured one upon the other, or if they are attached from the hand or foot above the middle joint and he cut them to separate them, that he is disqualified?

notes.he: למעלה דברייתא היינו למטה דמתני':
notes.en: “Above” in the baraita is the same as “below” in the mishna.

notes.dh: למעלה מן הפרק דאמר בגמרא היינו למטה מן הפרק דאמרינן במתני'
notes.he: או דמרבי כולהי הני מאו:
notes.en: “Above the joint” said in the Gemara is the same as “below the joint” that we say in the mishna. Or [the baraita] includes all of these from “or.”

messages.text: But didn’t you say in the mishna that if he separates his fingers he is fit? Rather, the baraita is referring to a priest whose fingers or toes are attached above the middle joint and he did not cut them.
messages.lead: The Gemara interrupts its citation of the baraita to ask:
messages.quote: above the middle joint and he cut them

messages.text: From where is it derived that he is disqualified? The verse states: “Or broken-handed.”

The mishna teaches: In a case where there was an extra finger or toe on his hand or foot and he cut it, if that extra appendage contains a bone, the priest is disqualified even after it was cut, as he is considered to be missing a limb, and if not, the priest is fit.
messages.quote: there was an extra finger or toe on his hand or foot and he cut it

messages.text: And this is the halakha only in a case where it can be counted along the back of the hand or foot, i.e., the extra digit is situated in a row with his other fingers or toes. Only in such a situation is an additional appendage considered a distinct limb to the extent that if it contains a bone he is disqualified even after it has been cut away.

notes.he: שנספרת עם שאר האצבעות שעומדת בשורתן בההיא קתני מתני' דחשיב אבר:
notes.en: And when it is counted along the back of the hand: it is counted with the other fingers, standing in their row. That is the case the mishna teaches, since then it counts as a limb.

notes.he: [ובנספרת] על גב היד שעומ' בשורת האצבעו':
notes.en: [And when it is counted] along the back of the hand: it stands in the row of the fingers.

messages.text: With regard to extra appendages the Sages taught:

In the case of an extra appendage that was cut from a corpse, which contains a bone, then even if it does not have a nail it imparts ritual impurity both through contact and by carrying it, and it imparts impurity in a tent, as is the halakha with regard to the limb of a corpse.

notes.dh: אם היה בה עצם ואין [בה] צפורן
notes.he: רבותא נקט אע"ג דאין בה צפורן חשיב אבר אם נספרת ע"ג היד:
notes.en: If it had a bone and no nail: [the baraita] states the greater novelty: even though it has no nail, it counts as a limb if it is counted along the back of the hand.

notes.he: וכגון שיש בה בשר קצת ולא כזית דאי הוה בה כזית בשר אפי' אינה נספרת או אין בה עצם נמי הוה מטמא באהל דהא כזית מן המת מטמא באהל ואי לא הוה בשר כלל אפילו נספרת נמי דחשיב אבר לא מטמא באהל דאין עצמות מטמאין באהל אלא רוב בנין או רוב מנין או רובע הקב אבל השתא דאיכא מקצת בשר מטמא אע"ג דליכא כזית הואיל ונספרת על גב היד דחשיב אבר דהכי אמרינן במס' נדה בפרק יוצא דופן (נדה דף מג:) האברים אין להם שיעור אפילו פחות מכזית מן הנבילה ופחות מכזית מן המת:
notes.en: It imparts impurity by contact, by carrying and in a tent: for example, where it has a little flesh, but not an olive’s bulk. For if it had an olive’s bulk of flesh, it would impart impurity in a tent even if it were not counted [with the fingers] or had no bone, since an olive’s bulk of a corpse imparts impurity in a tent. And if it had no flesh at all, then even if it were counted, so that it counts as a limb, it would not impart impurity in a tent, since bones impart impurity in a tent only as a majority of the skeleton, a majority of the number of bones, or a quarter-kav. But now that there is a little flesh, it imparts impurity even without an olive’s bulk, since it is counted along the back of the hand and counts as a limb. For so we say in Tractate Niddah, chapter Yotze Dofen (Niddah 43b): limbs have no minimum size; even less than an olive’s bulk of an animal carcass, or less than an olive’s bulk of a corpse [imparts impurity].

messages.text: And if the extra appendage has no flesh surrounding the bone and therefore does not impart the impurity of a limb from a corpse, it is included in the count of 125 bones, which constitute a majority of the number of bones in a human being. A majority of bones imparts impurity in a tent, even if there is no flesh on any of them.

notes.he: אם אין בה בשר עולה למנין קכ"ה דזהו רוב מנין אברי המת דאברי המת רמ"ח ורוב מנינו של מת מטמא באהל. ובנספרת דאי לא קיימא בשורת האצבעות לא חשיב אבר הואיל ואין בה צפורן:
notes.en: And it is included in the count of 125: if it has no flesh, it is included in the count of 125, which is a majority of the number of a corpse’s limbs, since a corpse has 248 limbs, and a majority of the number of a corpse’s [limbs] imparts impurity in a tent. And when it is counted: if it does not stand in the row of the fingers, it does not count as a limb, since it has no nail.

notes.he: אברים דהיינו רוב מנינו דרמ"ח אברים יש באדם:
notes.en: And it is included in the count of 125: limbs, which is a majority of the number of the 248 limbs a person has.

messages.text: And it is considered a limb only when it can be counted along the back of the hand or foot.
messages.quote: and it imparts impurity in a tent

messages.text: This matter was stated by our great rabbi, Rav, may the Omnipresent come to his assistance. An extra appendage that contains a bone and does not have a nail imparts ritual impurity through contact and by carrying, but it does not impart impurity in a tent.

notes.he: רב:
notes.en: Our great rabbi: Rav.

notes.he: רבי:
notes.en: Our great rabbi: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi. Rashi identifies him as Rav].

messages.text: And it does not impart impurity in a tent only when it is not counted along the back of the hand or foot.
messages.quote: but it does not impart impurity in a tent

notes.he: ובאינה נספרת כדמפ' דאיכא תרתי לגריעותא אין בה צפורן ואינה נספרת אבל יש בה צפורן מטמאה ואע"ג דאינה נספרת והכי תנן בפ' בא סימן (נדה דף מט.):
notes.en: But it does not impart impurity in a tent: this is where it is not counted, as [Rabbi Yoḥanan] explains, so that it has two shortcomings: it has no nail and it is not counted. But if it has a nail, it imparts impurity [in a tent] even though it is not counted; and so we learned in the chapter Ba Siman (Niddah 49a).

messages.text: The Sages rendered their statements in this case like statements of prophecy, i.e., there is no rationale for this halakha, as whichever way you look at it there is a difficulty: If a digit that is not counted with the other digits is considered a limb, it should impart impurity in a tent as well; and if it is not a limb, it also should not impart impurity through contact or by carrying.

notes.he: שאין צריכין ליתן טעם לנבואתן לפי שבלא טעם שומעים להם כך הם לא נתנו טעם לדבריהם:
notes.en: Like statements of prophecy: prophets need not give a reason for their prophecy, since people listen to them without a reason; so too, they gave no reason for their statement.

notes.dh: עשו דבריהם דברי נביאות מה נפשך כו'
notes.he: מדפריך עליה משמע דלאו לשבח קא"ל דברי נביאות ופ"ק דב"ב (דף יב. ושם) משמע דקאמר לענין חשיבות דמייתי עלה ההיא דאע"פ [שניטלה] נבואה מן הנביאים ובסוף כיצד מעברין (עירובין דף ס: ד"ה אין) פירשתי:
notes.en: They rendered their statements like statements of prophecy, whichever way you look at it: since [the Gemara] raises a difficulty with it, this implies that “statements of prophecy” was not said in praise. But in the first chapter of Bava Batra (12a) it implies that it is said in the sense of importance, since it cites there [the teaching] that even though prophecy was taken from the prophets [it was not taken from the Sages]. I have explained this at the end of the chapter Keitzad Me’abberin (Eruvin 60b).

notes.he: שאין אדם יודע לפרש מה טעם מטמא במגע ובמשא ואינו מטמא באהל:
notes.en: They rendered their statements like statements of prophecy: no one knows how to explain the reason why it imparts impurity by contact and carrying but not in a tent.

messages.text: This appendage imparts impurity through contact and by carrying because the Sages touched upon it, i.e., issued a ruling concerning it, and determined that the halakhot of a bone the volume of a barley grain apply to it, i.e., it is considered a bone fragment and not a limb. Accordingly, it does not impart impurity in a tent.

notes.he: דעצם כשעורה מטמא במגע ובמשא ואינו מטמא באהל אף האי נמי:
notes.en: They touched upon it because of a bone the size of a barley grain: a bone the size of a barley grain imparts impurity by contact and carrying and not in a tent; so too this one.

messages.text: It is a rabbinic decree that an appendage that is not counted with the other digits imparts impurity through contact and carrying, due to a case where the appendage is counted with the other digits, in which case it is considered a limb and imparts impurity in a tent.

notes.he: רב פפא אמר הואיל ואינה נספרת בדין הוא דאפילו במגע ובמשא נמי לא תטמא אלא גזירה שאינה נספרת דתטמא אטו נספרת:
notes.en: Rav Pappa says: since it is not counted, by right it should not impart impurity even by contact and carrying; but it is a decree that one that is not counted imparts impurity because of one that is counted.

messages.text: If so, then an appendage that is not counted should impart impurity in a tent as well.
messages.quote: decree that an appendage that is not counted

notes.he: ליגזור כשאינה נספרת דתטמא באהל אטו נספרת:
notes.en: If so: let them decree that one that is not counted imparts impurity in a tent because of one that is counted.

messages.text: The Sages implemented a distinction by decreeing this appendage imparts impurity only through contact and carrying, in order that people will know that this impurity applies by rabbinic law and not by Torah law. And therefore they will not come to burn teruma, i.e., the portion of produce designated for the priest, or consecrated items that have been rendered impure on account of this type of impurity, as by Torah law they are ritually pure and may not be burned.

notes.he: בה היכירא דלא תטמא באהל כי היכי דלא לישרפו על טומאתו תרומה וקדשים:
notes.en: They made a distinction with it: that it does not impart impurity in a tent, so that teruma and consecrated items will not be burned because of its impurity.

messages.caption: An extra digit from a corpse: when it imparts impurity, and the three explanations of the middle case.

messages.text: With regard to impurity imparted by extra appendages, we learned in a mishna there (Oholot 2:1):
A majority of the skeletal structure or a majority of the number of bones in the corpse of a dead person, even when there is not a quarter of a kav of bones among them, are impure.

notes.dh: ואע"פ שאין בהם רובע הקב טמאים
notes.he: באהל וגבי אהלות תנינן לה:
notes.en: And even though there is not a quarter-kav among them, they are impure: in a tent. It is taught in connection with [Tractate] Oholot.

notes.he: הקב של עצמות טמאין באהל:
notes.en: Even though there is not a quarter: a quarter-kav of bones among them, they impart impurity in a tent.

messages.text: Concerning the ruling of this mishna, the Sages taught in a baraita:

What is considered a majority of the skeletal structure of a corpse? It is two calves and one thigh, since this constitutes a majority of the height of an adult. What is considered a majority of the number of bones? One hundred and twenty-five bones.

notes.he: דזהו רוב הגובה באדם גדול שאינו ננס באברים דשני שוקיים וירך אחד הוי רוב גובה הגוף בלא הראש דלגבי בנין המת לא חשיב ראשו בברייתא דאהלות דקתני איזהו בנינו השוקיים והירכיים הגוף והשדרה. נ"א הואיל ורוב בנינו בגודל גרסינן והכי לישנא דתוספתא. בגודל בגובה:
notes.en: Since this is a majority of the height of an adult: a majority of the height of a grown person whose limbs are not dwarfed. For two shins and one thigh are a majority of the height of the body without the head, since the head is not counted in the structure of a corpse, in the baraita of Oholot that teaches: What is its structure? The shins and the thighs, the body and the spine. Another version: we read “since a majority of its structure is in height [ba-godel],” and that is the wording of the Tosefta. Ba-godel: in height.

notes.he: הואיל ויש רוב בנינו בגובהו של אדם:
notes.en: Two shins and one thigh: since this is a majority of a person’s structure in height.

messages.text: @Rava Is the tanna coming to teach us a number? It is obvious that as there are 248 bones in the human body, 125 of them constitute a majority.
messages.quote: One hundred and twenty-five bones

notes.he: בתמיה. דכיון דרמ"ח אברים פשיטא דרובא הוי קכ"ה:
notes.en: Is the tanna coming to teach us a number? Asked in surprise: since there are 248 limbs, it is obvious that 125 are a majority.

messages.text: The tanna teaches us that the halakha is as it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: Is the tanna coming to teach us a number?

messages.text: With regard to a corpse that lacks some bones and has only 200 bones, or one that has extra and has 281 bones, all of them are included in the count of 125. In other words, whether the number of 125 is in a majority or minority of that particular corpse, this number of bones imparts impurity, as one follows the majority of people, and most people have 248 bones.

notes.he: שנברא חסר בכל יד ובכל רגל ב' אצבעות דהיינו ח' אצבעות ובכל אצבע יש ו' עצמות כך מפרש במס' אהלות הרי חסר מן האצבעות מ"ח ולא נשתיירו אלא מאתים. ויתר שיש בו רפ"א כגון אשה שנבראת יתירה ד' אצבעות בכל יד ורגל והרי ד' אצבעות יתירין הוי כ"ד עצמות יותר ובאשה יש ב' צירין ושני דלתות ומפתח כדאמרינן לקמן הרי כ"ט אברין יותר הוסיפן על רמ"ח ותמצא רע"ז וד' הנותרין לא ידענא היכי מתרמי דודאי אין בכל אצבע אלא ו' עצמות סך הכל לא שורש ולא ענף והכי מפרש באהלות:
notes.en: Lacking, with only 200: one who was created lacking two fingers on each hand and each foot, that is, eight fingers; and each finger has six bones, as is explained in Tractate Oholot. So 48 are missing from the fingers, and only 200 remain. And extra, with 281: for example, a woman who was created with four extra fingers on her hands and feet. Four extra fingers are 24 more bones, and a woman has two hinges, two doors and a key, as we say below. That makes 29 extra limbs; add them to 248 and you have 277. As for the remaining four, I do not know how they come about, for each finger certainly has only six bones in all and nothing more [literally, “neither root nor branch”], and so it is explained in Oholot.

notes.he: כל אלו יתירין חשובין לאברים ועולין למנין קכ"ה ושמעינן מינה דאע"ג דקכ"ה לא הוי רובא דידיה דהא רפ"א היו לו אפ"ה הוי קכ"ה רובא וגבי חסר נמי אע"ג דהוי רובא דידיה [ק"א] אפ"ה לא חשיב רובא אלא קכ"ה:
notes.en: All of them are included in the count of 125: all these extras count as limbs and are included in the count of 125. And we learn from this that even though 125 is not a majority of this one’s limbs, since he had 281, nevertheless 125 counts as a majority. And with the one who is lacking, too: even though [101] would be a majority of his, nevertheless only 125 counts as a majority.

notes.he: אדם חסר שאין בו אלא מאתים אברים כגון שחסר מכל יד ומכל רגל ב' אצבעות ובכל אצבע יש בו שש עצמות עד הזרוע דהיינו חסר מ"ח אברים:
notes.en: Lacking: a person lacking, who has only 200 limbs, for example, one who is missing two fingers from each hand and each foot; each finger has six bones up to the arm, so he is missing 48 limbs.

notes.dh: ויתיר שיש בו מאתים ושמונים ואחד
notes.he: שזה יש לו ל"ג אברים יותר ואלו הן שיש לו ד' אצבעות יתירות בידיו וברגליו שיש בהן כ"ד אברים ולכל השש עצמות שבכל אצבע יש כנגדו בזרוע עצם אחד היינו כ"ח יתירות:
notes.en: And extra, who has 281: this one has 33 extra limbs, and these are they: he has four extra fingers on his hands and feet, which have 24 limbs; and for each set of six bones in a finger there is one corresponding bone in the arm, making 28 extras.

notes.he: והיינו רפ"א אברים:
notes.en: And two hinges, two doors and a key: and that makes 281 limbs.

notes.he: אפילו הנך יתירות עולין בחשבון קכ"ה דבין ליתיר ובין לחסר לא אזלינן בתר רוב אברים דידהו אלא בתר רוב אברים דאינשי דעלמא דהוי קכ"ה:
notes.en: All of them are included in the count of 125: even these extras are included in the reckoning of 125, for with the extra and the lacking alike we do not follow the majority of their own limbs but the majority of the limbs of ordinary people, which is 125.

messages.text: The printed text reads “Rabbi Yehuda” here. Since he cites the Amora Shmuel, this is presumably Rav Yehuda, Shmuel’s student.

With regard to the number of limbs or bones in the human body, there was an incident involving the students of Rabbi Yishmael, who boiled the corpse of a prostitute who was sentenced by the king to death by burning, in order to separate her flesh from her bones. They examined and found she had 252 limbs. They were puzzled by their finding, as the Sages say that the human body has only 248 limbs.
Shmuel said to them: Perhaps you examined the corpse of a woman, as the verse added to her two hinges and two doors, for a total of 252 limbs.

notes.he: קרדונ"ש:
notes.en: Hinges [tzirin]: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita:
Just as a house has hinges [tzirim], so too, a woman has hinges, as it is stated: “And she bowed herself and brought forth, for her pains [tzireha] came suddenly upon her” (I Samuel 4:19).

verse.he: וְכַלָּתוֹ אֵשֶׁת־פִּינְחָס הָרָה לָלַת וַתִּשְׁמַע אֶת־הַשְּׁמוּעָה אֶל־הִלָּקַח אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים וּמֵת חָמִיהָ וְאִישָׁהּ וַתִּכְרַע וַתֵּלֶד כִּי־נֶהֶפְכוּ עָלֶיהָ צִרֶיהָ׃
verse.en: His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant, about to give birth. When she heard the report that the Ark of God was captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she was seized with labor pains, and she crouched down and gave birth.

messages.text: Just as a house has doors, so too, a woman has doors, as it is stated: “Because it did not shut the doors of my womb” (Job 3:10).

verse.he: כִּי לֹא סָגַר דַּלְתֵי בִטְנִי וַיַּסְתֵּר עָמָל מֵעֵינָי׃
verse.en:
Because it did not block my mother’s womb,
And hide trouble from my eyes.

messages.text: Just as there is a key to a house, so too, there is a key to a woman, as it is stated: “And He opened her womb” (Genesis 30:22).

verse.he: וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת־רָחֵל וַיִּשְׁמַע אֵלֶיהָ אֱלֹהִים וַיִּפְתַּח אֶת־רַחְמָהּ׃
verse.en: Now God remembered Rachel; God heeded her and opened her womb.

messages.text: The incident involving the students of Rabbi Yishmael, who found that the woman had only four additional limbs rather than five, i.e., there was no key, poses a difficulty for Rabbi Akiva.
messages.quote: a key to a woman

notes.he: מפתח הוו להו רנ"ג וקשיא לתלמידי ר' ישמעאל דלא מצאו אלא רנ"ב:
notes.en: For Rabbi Akiva: with the key, there would be 253, which is difficult in light of Rabbi Yishmael’s students, who found only 252.

notes.he: לר' עקיבא קשיא דתלמידי דרבי ישמעאל דאינהו לא אשכחו אלא ד' אברים טפי באדם ורבי עקיבא דמוסיף מפתח איכא ה' אברים טפי:
notes.en: The [incident of] Rabbi Yishmael’s students is difficult for Rabbi Akiva: they found only four limbs more in a person, while for Rabbi Akiva, who adds a key, there are five limbs more.

messages.text: Perhaps since it is small, it dissolved in the water when they boiled the corpse.

notes.he: המפתח איתמוחי איתמח מחמת שליקה:
notes.en: Since it is small: the key dissolved because of the boiling.

notes.he: ההוא עצם דמפתח איתמוח איתמח בששלקוה:
notes.en: Perhaps since it is small: that bone of the key dissolved when they boiled it.

messages.text: And all of them, i.e., all the limbs found only in a woman, do not impart impurity in a tent, as it is stated: “This is the law: When a person dies in a tent” (Numbers 19:14), indicating that only an item that is equal for all people, male and female, imparts impurity in a tent.

verse.he: זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי־יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל כׇּל־הַבָּא אֶל־הָאֹהֶל וְכׇל־אֲשֶׁר בָּאֹהֶל יִטְמָא שִׁבְעַת יָמִים׃
verse.en: This is the ritual: When a person dies in a tent, whoever enters the tent and whoever is in the tent shall be impure seven days;

notes.he: כל היתירין הללו שבאשה אין מטמאין באהל האבר בפני עצמו שיש עליו בשר קצת:
notes.en: And all of them: all these extra [limbs] in a woman do not impart impurity in a tent as a limb on its own with a little flesh on it.

notes.he: הני חמשה יתירי אינן מטמאין באהל כו':
notes.en: And all of them: these five extras do not impart impurity in a tent.

messages.text: And are there no hinges in a man? But isn’t it written: “Pangs [tzirim] have taken hold upon me, as the pangs of a woman in travail” (Isaiah 21:3)?
messages.quote: an item that is equal for all people, male and female

verse.he: עַל־כֵּן מָלְאוּ מׇתְנַי חַלְחָלָה צִירִים אֲחָזוּנִי כְּצִירֵי יוֹלֵדָה נַעֲוֵיתִי מִשְּׁמֹעַ נִבְהַלְתִּי מֵרְאוֹת׃
verse.en:
Therefore my loins
Are seized with trembling;
I am gripped by pangs
Like a woman in travail,
Too anguished to hear,
Too frightened to see.

messages.text: The verse is referring specifically to hinges of flesh, which are not considered limbs, as they contain no bones.

notes.he: תירוצא הוא. לא חשיב אבר בלא עצם:
notes.en: Hinges of flesh: this is an answer. Without a bone it does not count as a limb.

notes.he: וליכא בהו עצמות:
notes.en: Hinges of flesh: and there are no bones in them.

messages.text: But isn’t it written: “My lord, by reason of the vision my pains [tzirai] come” (Daniel 10:16)?

verse.he: וְהִנֵּה כִּדְמוּת בְּנֵי אָדָם נֹגֵעַ עַל־שְׂפָתָי וָאֶפְתַּח־פִּי וָאֲדַבְּרָה וָאֹמְרָה אֶל־הָעֹמֵד לְנֶגְדִּי אֲדֹנִי בַּמַּרְאָה נֶהֶפְכוּ צִירַי עָלַי וְלֹא עָצַרְתִּי כֹּחַ׃
verse.en: Then [this figure] who looked human touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and spoke, saying to him who stood before me, “My lord, because of the vision, I have been seized with pangs and cannot summon strength.

messages.text: Here too, the verse is referring to hinges of flesh.

So too, it is reasonable that the hinges of a male are only of flesh, as if you do not say so, then as far as the 248 limbs that the Sages stated constitute a human body, how can you find them? Neither in a man nor in a woman.

notes.he: דלית בהו עצמות בצירי דאי לא תימא הכי כו':
notes.en: So too it is reasonable: that there are no bones in the hinges [of a man], for if you do not say so…

messages.text: And both derived their opinions from one verse, as it is stated with regard to David’s war against the Philistines: “And there was again war at Gath” (II Samuel 21:20), and it is also written in that same verse: “And there was a champion, who had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, twenty-four in number.”
messages.quote: an extra appendage on his hands and on his feet, six on each for a total of twenty-four

verse.he: וַתְּהִי־עוֹד מִלְחָמָה בְּגַת וַיְהִי ׀ אִישׁ (מדין) [מָדוֹן] וְאֶצְבְּעֹת יָדָיו וְאֶצְבְּעֹת רַגְלָיו שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע מִסְפָּר וְגַם־הוּא יֻלַּד לְהָרָפָה׃
verse.en: Once again there was fighting, at Gath. There was a giant of a man, in light of 1 Chron. 20.6; meaning of Heb. uncertain. Or “an adversary,” following the qere; cf. Gersonides. who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all; he too was descended from the Raphah.

messages.text: One Sage, i.e., the Rabbis, holds that the verse speaks of negative qualities of the champion, and therefore it may be derived from here that extra appendages are blemishes; and one Sage, Rabbi Yehuda, holds that the verse speaks in his praise, which means that extra appendages are not blemishes at all.

Why do I need that which is written in the verse: “On every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, twenty-four in number”? Isn’t it obvious that one who has six appendages on each limb will have twenty-four in total?

All of these details are necessary, as, had the Merciful One written only six and six, I would say there were six of his hand and six of his foot, i.e., he had only twelve appendages. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote “twenty-four.”

notes.he: בידו אחת וברגלו אחת היה יתר ולא בשתיהן:
notes.en: Six of his and six of his foot: he had extras on one hand and on one foot, and not on both.

notes.he: חדא ושית דכרעיה חדא:
notes.en: I would say six of his: one [hand], and six of his foot: one [foot].

messages.text: And had the Merciful One written only “twenty-four,” I would say he had five fingers on this side and seven fingers on that side. Therefore, the verse wrote six and six. The verse concludes with the term “in number” to indicate that these fingers were counted in a single row on the back of the hand.
With regard to the dispute concerning whether or not extra appendages are a blemish, it is taught in a baraita:

There was an incident involving one man who came before Rabbi Tarfon, and he had extra appendages on his hands and on his feet, six and six, for a total of twenty-four appendages. Rabbi Tarfon said to him: There should increase among the Jewish people those that are like you, i.e., strong men. Clearly, extra appendages are not a blemish but a praiseworthy condition.

@Rabbi Yehuda You seek to bring a proof from there? This is what Rabbi Tarfon actually said to him: All mamzerim and Gibeonites should be like you, i.e., physically weak, so that they should decrease from the Jewish people.
messages.quote: There should increase among the Jewish people those that are like you

notes.he: כל ממזרים שבישראל יהיו כמותך ויהיו ניכרין שמטפה פסולה הן ולא ידבקו בהן:
notes.en: Like you, may mamzerim and Gibeonites decrease from Israel: may all the mamzerim in Israel be like you, so that they are recognizable as coming from unfit seed, and [people] will not cling to them [in marriage].

notes.dh: משם ראיה דלא אמר ליה כמותך ירבו משום שבחא
notes.he: אלא כך אמר ליה כמותך ירבו אצבעות יתירות בממזירי ונתיני שבישראל כדי שיהו ניכרין ויתמעטו שיפרשו ישראל מהן מלהתחתן בם:
notes.en: Is that a proof? He did not say to him “may there increase [those] like you” as praise. Rather, he said to him: like you, may extra fingers increase among the mamzerim and Gibeonites in Israel, so that they are recognizable and decrease, as Israel will keep away from marrying them.

messages.text: With regard to this dispute the Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: who is ambidextrous and has control of both of his hands

messages.text: One whose left side is dominant, whether his left hand or his left foot, is disqualified from performing the Temple service. Furthermore, in the case of one who has control of both of his hands, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi deems him disqualified and the Rabbis deem him fit.

notes.he: שכשמהלך עוקר רגל השמאל תחלה מה שאין דרך בני אדם כך. איטר ביד פסול דכתי' וטבל אצבעו כל מקום שנא' אצבע וכהן אינו אלא ימין (זבחים דף כד.) ואיטר דרגל נמי לעמוד ולשרת כתי' כדרך שאר עמידה דעיקרו בימין:
notes.en: Left-handed in the foot: when he walks he lifts the left foot first, which is not the way of people. One who is left-handed in the hand is disqualified, as it is written: “And he shall dip his finger,” and wherever “finger” and “priest” are stated, it means only the right (Zevaḥim 24a). And one who is left-footed [is disqualified] too, since it is written “to stand to serve,” in the manner of all standing, which rests mainly on the right.

messages.text: One Sage, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, holds that he learned to control his left hand because a weakness began in his right hand. He is therefore disqualified, as his right hand is weak. And one Sage, i.e., the Rabbis, holds that a strength began in his left hand that allowed him to control both hands. Nevertheless, his right hand remains strong.

notes.he: ליה בימין:
notes.en: As one Sage holds that a weakness began: in his right [hand].

notes.he: ר' דפוסל כחישותא אתחלא ליה בימין שהרי אין כוחה יתר משמאל והוי מום:
notes.en: One Sage holds: Rabbi, who disqualifies him [holds that] a weakness began in his right hand, since its strength is no greater than the left’s, and that is a blemish.

messages.text: Mishna

Concerning the kushi, the giḥor, the lavkan, the kipe’aḥ, the dwarf, the deaf-mute, the imbecile, the drunk, and those with ritually pure marks, their conditions disqualify a person from performing the Temple service and are valid, i.e., they do not disqualify with regard to being sacrificed, in the case of an animal.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Mishna. The kushi, the giḥor, the lavkan and the kipe’aḥ: explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: כגון ספחת. דאי נגעים טמאים לא איצטריך למימר דאפילו אכניסה דעזרה הוי חייב כרת:
notes.en: And those with pure marks: for example, a sappaḥat [a type of skin mark]. For impure marks need not be stated, since [such a person] would be liable to karet even for entering the Temple courtyard.

messages.text: An imbecile among animals is not optimal for sacrifice.
Even with regard to those with flesh or skin that hangs from their body, that blemish disqualifies in the case of a person and is valid in the case of an animal.

notes.he: כמין חתיכות בשר יוצאות ותולות להם:
notes.en: Taltulin: like pieces of flesh that protrude and hang from them. [Rashi’s text reads taltulin where the printed mishna reads dildulin.]

messages.text: Gemara
A kushi is one whose skin is extremely black, a giḥor is one whose skin is extremely white, and a lavkan is one whose skin is extremely red.
messages.quote: the kushi, the giḥor, the lavkan

messages.text: Is that so? But there was a certain person who said to others: Who wants a lukiyani lamb, and the lamb was found to be white.
messages.quote: a lavkan is one whose skin is extremely red

messages.text: Rather, a kushi is one whose skin is extremely black; a giḥor is one whose skin is extremely red, as people say about one whose skin is extremely red: Giḥia red; and a lavkan is one whose skin is extremely white, as in the case of that person who said: Who wants a lukiyani, and it was found to be white.

notes.he: רו"ש בלעז:
notes.en: Gemara. Sumka [red]: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: טלאים לבנים היו: לסומקא רגילי אינשי למיקרייה גוהיא:
notes.en: Lukiyani: they were white lambs. People customarily call a red one gohya.

notes.he: אדום ביותר:
notes.en: Sumka gihya: extremely red.

messages.text: This is referring to one who is extremely tall.
messages.lead: The mishna teaches that a kipe’aḥ is disqualified. Rav Zevid taught:
messages.quote: the kipe’aḥ

messages.text: Is that so, that one who is tall is considered blemished? But didn’t Rabbi Abbahu teach:
messages.quote: extremely tall

messages.text: From where is it derived that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is praised through His destruction of those of stature? As it is stated: “Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars” (Amos 2:9).

verse.he: וְאָנֹכִי הִשְׁמַדְתִּי אֶת־הָאֱמֹרִי מִפְּנֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר כְּגֹבַהּ אֲרָזִים גׇּבְהוֹ וְחָסֹן הוּא כָּאַלּוֹנִים וָאַשְׁמִיד פִּרְיוֹ מִמַּעַל וְשׇׁרָשָׁיו מִתָּחַת׃
verse.en:
Yet I
Destroyed the Amorite before them,
Whose stature was like the cedar’s
And who was stout as the oak,
Destroying his boughs above
And his trunk below!

messages.text: The mishna is not referring to one who is tall and has a healthy build, but to one who is long, emaciated, and ugly.

notes.he: דארוך הוא ודק שאינו עבה לפי אורכו ולפי שדק הוא אינו יכול לסבול קומתו ונכפף ונראה כמו שחליותיו שמוטות:
notes.en: Long, emaciated [shemita], ugly: he is tall and thin, not broad in proportion to his height; and because he is thin he cannot bear his height, so he stoops and looks as if his vertebrae have slipped [shemutot].

notes.he: ארוך ודק ופרצופו בולט הרבה לחוץ וסנוי הוא לראות הוי מום:
notes.en: Be’arikha shamuta sanya: long and thin, with a face that juts far outward, and unpleasant to look at; this is a blemish.

messages.text: A man who is tall should not marry a woman who is also tall, lest there emerge from them a child who is extremely tall. Similarly, a man who is a dwarf should not marry a woman who is also a dwarf, lest there emerge from them a child who is exceptionally short.

A man whose skin is pale should not marry a woman whose skin is also pale, lest there emerge from them a child who is extremely pale. Likewise, a man whose skin is dark should not marry a woman whose skin is also dark, lest there emerge from them a child who is extremely dark.

notes.he: שלבן ביותר:
notes.en: Bohak [rendered “pale”]: very white.

notes.he: שחור כקדירה וחבירו בשילהי מס' שבת (דף קנז.) ופקקו את המאור בטפיח:
notes.en: Tafuaḥ [rendered “dark”]: black as a pot. Similarly, at the end of Tractate Shabbat (157a): “and they stopped up the skylight with a tefiaḥ [an earthenware vessel].”

notes.he: לבן הוא יותר מדאי דהוי נגע:
notes.en: Bohak: excessively white, which is a [skin] mark.

messages.text: Since one who is drunk profanes the Temple service, the blemish of drunkenness should have been counted in the previous chapter together with those who have blemishes that profane the service. By contrast, those listed in this mishna are disqualified only because they are not equal among the seed of Aaron, and the halakha is that rites performed by priests with such blemishes are not profaned after the fact (see 43b).
messages.quote: the deaf-mute, the imbecile, the drunk

notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: A drunk? Asked in surprise.

notes.he: דכתיב (ויקרא י) יין ושכר אל תשת וכתיב בתריה להבדיל בין הקודש ובין החול וגו':
notes.en: He profanes the service: as it is written: “Drink no wine nor strong drink” (Leviticus 10:9), and after it: “And that you may put difference between the holy and the common.”

notes.he: גמורין בעי למיחשביה וקתני ליה גבי מומין הבאין מחמת שאין שוין בזרעו של אהרן דאמרינן בריש פירקין דלא מחלי עבודה:
notes.en: Together with the blemishes: it should have been counted with the full blemishes, yet it is taught with the blemishes that disqualify because one is not equal among the seed of Aaron, about which we said at the start of our chapter that they do not profane the service.

notes.he: בהדי מומי בעי למיחשביה משום דכולהו דמתני' לאו מומין נינהו אלא משום דאין שוה בזרע של אהרן הוא דאסור. שיכור מחיל עבודה מפורש במסכת זבחים:
notes.en: Tefiaḥ: an earthenware vessel, black. [On the drunk:] it should have been counted with the blemishes, since all those in the mishna are not blemishes but are forbidden only because one is not equal among the seed of Aaron. A drunk profanes the service, as is explained in Tractate Zevaḥim.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to a case where one became drunk through other intoxicating agents, not through wine. In such a case, the rites are not profaned. And this is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who holds that even in such a case the rites are profaned, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דמשוי לשאר דברים המשכרים דין יין דמחלי עבודה דקאמר במס' כריתות (דף יג:) על היין במיתה ועל שאר משכרין באזהרה ונפקא לן משכר אל תשת וכתיב בתריה ולהבדיל בין הקדש ובין החול אלמא לרבי יהודה שאר משכרין מחלי עבודה:
notes.en: And not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: who gives other intoxicants the status of wine, which profanes the service. As it says in Tractate Keritot (13b): for wine, [the penalty is] death, and for other intoxicants, a prohibition; and we derive it from “strong drink, do not drink,” after which it is written, “and that you may put difference between the holy and the common.” Evidently, according to Rabbi Yehuda other intoxicants profane the service.

notes.dh: ובשאר דברים המשכרים ודלא כר' יהודה
notes.he: הא דתניא בסוף פ"ק דזבחים (דף יד:) זר ואונן ושיכור ובעלי מום בקבלה ובהולכה ובזריקה פסול יש לתמוה אמאי נקט שיכור הוה ליה למימר שתויי יין ופרועי ראש ואומר החכם ר' חיים כהן נ"ע דמיירי בשאר דברים המשכרים וכר' יהודה דמחיל עבודה כדמוקמינן שיכור דהכא בשאר דברים המשכרים:
notes.en: Through other intoxicating agents, and not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: in what is taught at the end of the first chapter of Zevaḥim (14b), that a non-priest, an acute mourner, a drunk and a blemished priest disqualify [the blood] in receiving, carrying and sprinkling, one may wonder why it mentions “a drunk”; it should have said “those who drank wine” and “those with overgrown hair.” The sage Rabbi Ḥayyim Kohen, may his soul rest in Eden, says that it speaks of other intoxicating agents and follows Rabbi Yehuda, who holds that [such a priest] profanes the service, just as we establish the drunk here as one [made drunk] by other intoxicating agents.

notes.dh: בשאר המשכרין דלר' יהודה במיתה ולרבנן באזהרה ופלוגתייהו בסיפרא
notes.he: דלדולין תלתול:
notes.en: Through other intoxicants: for according to Rabbi Yehuda [the penalty is] death, and according to the Rabbis, a prohibition; their dispute is in the Sifra. [A note by the printed edition’s editor adds here: this is also the view of the Rambam, that a priest drunk from other intoxicants who served would be flogged; yet Keritot 13b implies that according to the Rabbis and Rabbi Elazar there is not even a prohibition; see the Kesef Mishneh on chapter 1 of Hilkhot Bi’at HaMikdash, and the matter requires further study.] [Rabbeinu Gershom then glosses the mishna’s word:] Dildulin: a wart [taltul].

messages.text: A priest who ate pressed figs from Ke’ila or drank milk or honey, thereby becoming intoxicated, and entered the Sanctuary to serve, is liable to receive lashes.

notes.he: הגדילה באותו מקום ומשכרת כיין:
notes.en: As it is taught: one who ate pressed figs of Ke’ila: which grow in that place and intoxicate like wine.

notes.he: מי"ד בלע"ז מים ודבש שלוקין ביחד חייב מלקות כר' יהודה מוקמינן לה בפרק אמרו לו בכריתות (שם) דקאמר התם על שאר משכרין באזהרה דאל תשת דכיון דכתיבי שאר משכרין מחלי עבודה דהא כתיב בין הקודש ובין החול ומתני' דלא חשיב להו גבי הנך דמחלי עבודה דלא כר' יהודה:
notes.en: Honey: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), [that is,] water and honey boiled together. He is liable to lashes: we establish this as Rabbi Yehuda’s view in the chapter Amru Lo in Keritot (ibid.), where it says that for other intoxicants there is a prohibition from “do not drink.” Since other intoxicants are written [in the verse], they profane the service, for it is written “between the holy and the common.” And our mishna, which does not count them with those that profane the service, is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: This is because he transgressed the prohibition: “Drink no wine nor strong drink, you, nor your sons with you, when you go into the Tent of Meeting” (Leviticus 10:9). He understands that “strong drink” means any intoxicating agent. The verse indicates that one who performs the Temple service while drunk profanes the service, as it states immediately afterward: “And that you may put difference between the holy and the common.”

verse.he: יַיִן וְשֵׁכָר אַל־תֵּשְׁתְּ ׀ אַתָּה ׀ וּבָנֶיךָ אִתָּךְ בְּבֹאֲכֶם אֶל־אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְלֹא תָמֻתוּ חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: Drink no wine or other intoxicant, you or your sons, when you enter the Tent of Meeting, that you may not die. This is a law for all time throughout the ages,

messages.text: Mishna

These flaws do not disqualify a person from performing the Temple service, but they do disqualify an animal from being sacrificed: An animal whose mother or offspring were slaughtered that day, as slaughtering it would violate the prohibition against slaughtering the animal itself and its offspring on the same day; a tereifa; one born by caesarean section; one with which a transgression of bestiality was performed; and one that killed a person.

notes.he: פסול לקרבן דמחוסר זמן הוא:
notes.en: Mishna. Itself and its offspring: it is disqualified as an offering, since it is “lacking time” [and may not be offered until the next day].

notes.he: כהנים כשרים לעבודה ביחד וכן כהן טרפה ויוצא דופן כשר לעבודה:
notes.en: Itself and its offspring: [a father and son who are] priests are fit to serve together; and likewise a priest who is a tereifa, or was born by caesarean section, is fit for the service.

messages.text: And a priest who marries women by a transgression, e.g., a divorcée or a woman who underwent ḥalitza, is disqualified from performing the Temple service until he vows not to derive benefit from her. The vow ensures that he will divorce her promptly.

notes.he: גרושה וחלוצה:
notes.en: And one who marries women by a transgression: a divorcée or a ḥalutza.

notes.he: כגון אלמנה לכהן גדול וחלוצה לכהן הדיוט פסול עד שידור מהן הנאה שיגרשן:
notes.en: One who marries women by a transgression: for example, a widow to a High Priest, or a ḥalutza to an ordinary priest. He is disqualified until he vows not to benefit from them, so that he will divorce them.

messages.text: And a priest who becomes impure through exposure to corpses is disqualified from performing the Temple service until he accepts upon himself a commitment that he will no longer become impure through exposure to corpses.

messages.caption: The two mishnayot side by side: what disqualifies a priest but not an animal, and what disqualifies an animal but not a priest.

messages.text: Gemara
To what possible case involving people is the mishna referring when it differentiates between people and animals with regard to the flaw of: Itself and its offspring?
messages.quote: These flaws do not disqualify a person … itself and its offspring

messages.text: If we say this is referring to Aaron and his sons, and it means that they may serve in the Temple on the same day, then in the corresponding situation the mishna must be referring to a male goat and its offspring. And does such a prohibition apply? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:

The prohibition against slaughtering an animal itself and its offspring on the same day applies to female animals, i.e., a mother and its offspring, but it does not apply to males, i.e., a father and its offspring.

Rather, the mishna is referring to a female goat and its offspring, that they may not be slaughtered on the same day. If so, in the corresponding situation here, with regard to the priesthood, the mishna must be referring to a female priest and her son. But is a female priest fit for performing the Temple service at all? Clearly not.
Actually, the mishna is referring to Aaron and his sons, and in the corresponding situation here, it is referring to a male goat and its offspring.
That is to say, the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Ḥananya, as it is taught in a baraita:
messages.lead: And as for the difficulty that the prohibition of: Itself and its offspring, applies only to the mother, they said in the West, Eretz Yisrael, in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Avin:

notes.he: זאת אומרת:
notes.en: Gemara. Ada amra: this is to say.

messages.text: The prohibition against slaughtering an animal itself and its offspring on the same day applies to female animals but it does not apply to male animals.
It applies to both male and female animals.

notes.he: האב והבן או בת:
notes.en: In males: the father with the son or daughter.

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: who marries women by a transgression … until he vows not to derive benefit from her

messages.text: If a priest was performing a sacrificial rite and it was discovered that he married a woman who was forbidden to him, he does not stop performing the rite. Rather, he vows not to derive benefit from her and then continues to perform the rite. Once he has finished, he descends from the altar and divorces his wife.

notes.he: אע"פ שעדיין לא גירש מותר לעבוד משנדר שלא תהנה ממנו והוא ממנה:
notes.en: He vows and serves: even though he has not yet divorced her, he is permitted to serve once he has vowed that she will not benefit from him, nor he from her.

notes.he: נודר הנאה ועובד עבודתו על גבי המזבח ולכשירד מעבודתו מגרש דלא צריך לגרש קודם שיעבוד:
notes.en: He vows not to benefit and performs his service on the altar, and when he comes down from his service he divorces; he need not divorce before he serves.

messages.text: How can he be permitted to perform the Temple service before actually divorcing his wife? But let us be concerned that perhaps he will go before a Sage who will dissolve his vow.
messages.quote: he vows not to derive benefit from her and then continues to perform the rite

notes.he: דלא לישרייה לעבוד קודם שיגרש דלמא בתר דעבד עבודה אזיל לגבי חכם ושייל על נדריה ושרי ליה חכם ואישתכח דלא מגרש:
notes.en: But let us be concerned: [and so] not permit him to serve before he divorces, lest after he has performed the service he go to a Sage and ask about his vow, and the Sage release it, and it turns out that he does not divorce.

messages.text: The tanna holds that when one seeks to dissolve a vow, he must delineate the conditions of the vow to the Sage. Accordingly, when the Sage hears that he uttered this vow because he married a woman who was forbidden to him, the Sage will not dissolve it.

notes.he: הבא להתיר נדרו צריך שיפרט על מה נדר וכי שמע דמשום דפסולה לו נדר לא שרי נדריה:
notes.en: He must delineate: one who comes to have his vow dissolved must specify what he vowed about; and when [the Sage] hears that he vowed because she is unfit for him, he will not dissolve his vow.

notes.he: האי דאמר נודר ועובד קסבר דצריך לפרוט מה נדר וכיון דמפרש לחכם שנדר לגרש אשתו הפסולה לו לא קא שרי ליה חכם ההוא נדר:
notes.en: He holds: the one who says “he vows and serves” holds that one must specify what one vowed; and since he explains to the Sage that he vowed in order to divorce his wife who is unfit for him, the Sage will not release that vow.

messages.text: This works out well according to the one who says one must delineate the conditions of the vow. But according to the one who says he does not need to delineate the conditions of the vow, what can be said?

notes.he: פלוגתא היא דר"נ ורב פפא בפ' השולח (גיטין דף לה:) ונראה דהלכתא כר"פ דצריך לפרט דבתראה הוא ואפילו לפי הספרים דגרסי התם רב ששת במקום רב פפא אין הלכה כרב נחמן דלאו לענין דינא איתשיל להדין אלמנה הבאה לגבות כתובתה אלא לענין איסורא איתשיל כדמשמע התם דקאמר ואי אמרת דצריך לפרט זימנין דגזאן ליה לדיבוריה ורב הונא נמי שהוא גדול בחכמה ובמנין קסבר נמי התם צריך לפרט:
notes.en: This works out well according to the one who says one must delineate: this is a dispute between Rav Naḥman and Rav Pappa in the chapter HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 35b). It seems that the halakha follows Rav Pappa, that one must delineate, since he is the later authority. And even according to the texts there that read Rav Sheshet in place of Rav Pappa, the halakha does not follow Rav Naḥman [whose rulings are usually followed in monetary law], since that question was not raised as a monetary matter, about a widow who comes to collect her marriage contract, but as a matter of prohibition, as is implied there, where it says: “And if you say one must delineate, sometimes he will cut his words short.” And Rav Huna too, who is greater in wisdom and in years, holds there that one must delineate.

messages.text: That we administer the vow to the priest in public. Such a vow cannot be dissolved.

notes.he: ליה לפני רבים דמגרשה ולא מצי מיפר חכם:
notes.en: That we administer the vow: to him before the public, that he will divorce her, and a Sage cannot nullify it.

messages.text: This works out well according to the one who says that a vow that was taken in public has no option of nullification by a halakhic authority, but according to the one who says it has the option of nullification, what can be said?

notes.he: פלוגתא היא במס' גיטין (דף מו.) גבי המוציא את אשתו משום נדר בהשולח גט:
notes.en: A vow taken in public: this is a dispute in Tractate Gittin (46a), in the chapter HaSholeaḥ Get, concerning one who divorces his wife because of a vow.

notes.dh: הניחא למ"ד נדר שהודר ברבים אין לו הפרה
notes.he: פי' בקונט' פלוגתא במס' גיטין בהשולח גט לאשתו (דף מו.) גבי המוציא את אשתו משום נדר דקאמר ר' יהודה כל נדר שידעו בו רבים לא יחזיר דאיכא פריצותא שנדרה נדר שאין לו היתר ושלא ידעו בו רבים יחזיר דלא חייש לקלקולא וא"ת מנלן דפליגי רבנן עליה דרבי יהודה בהכי דקסברי יש לו הפרה דלמא בקלקולא לחוד פליגי ובההיא שמעתין דהתם נמי פשיטא ליה להש"ס דקסברי רבנן יש לו הפרה דקאמרי רבנן אטו התם מי חיילא שבועה עלייהו כלל וכי תימא מדלא מפלגי רבנן בין ידעו בו רבים ללא ידעו בכל ענין לא יחזיר דחיישינן לקלקולא אלמא יש לו הפרה הא לא מפלגי נמי בדעת הרבים ואע"ג דאיכא לפלוגי דמה נפשך אין לו הפרה לכ"ע ויש לפרש דעל דעת רבים לא איירי כלל לא אינהו ולא ר' יהודה אין לחוש אם לא פירשו אע"פ שיש לחלק אבל בהודר ברבים שחילק ר' יהודה אם איתא דאין לו הפרה לרבנן נמי הוה לפרושי לחלק ולומר איפכא מדרבי יהודה ועוד כי בעל דעת רבים איכא למימר שיש לו הפרה מדעתם של אותם רבים שנדר על דעתם או לדבר מצוה שיש לו הפרה ולהכי לא פסיק ליה למיתני בעל דעת רבים שיחזיר למאן דחייש לקלקולא דפעמים שיש לו היתר ואיכא קלקולא אבל ברבים אין לו הפרה לא שנא לדבר מצוה ולא שנא לדבר הרשות בשום ענין אין לו הפרה תדע דמעשה דגבעונים לדבר מצוה היה:
notes.en: In brief: Rashi located the dispute in Gittin 46a, where Rabbi Yehuda rules that one who divorced his wife because of a vow the public knew of may not remarry her, because of the impropriety [of a vow that cannot be released], while if the public did not know of it he may remarry her, since he is not concerned about a mishap. Tosafot ask how we know that the Rabbis there disagree and hold that a public vow can be nullified; perhaps they differ from Rabbi Yehuda only about the concern for a mishap. They answer that in that sugya the Talmud also takes it as obvious that the Rabbis hold it can be nullified, since the Rabbis ask whether the oath to the Gibeonites was binding at all. One might argue that since the Rabbis do not distinguish between a known and an unknown vow, the public vow must be nullifiable; but they also do not distinguish a vow taken on the consent of the public, which everyone agrees cannot be nullified. Tosafot answer that neither the Rabbis nor Rabbi Yehuda discussed the consent of the public at all, so their silence there proves nothing; but where Rabbi Yehuda did distinguish a vow made in public, the Rabbis would have had to say so had they agreed it cannot be nullified. Further, a vow on the consent of the public can sometimes be released, with the consent of those people or for a mitzva, so the mishna could not state flatly that the husband may remarry; whereas a vow in public, on this view, has no nullification at all, even for a mitzva, as the Gibeonite oath shows, which was for a mitzva. messages.text: That we administer the vow …

notes.he: וא"ת בריש השולח (גיטין דף לה:) גאלמנה שהתקין רבן שמעון בן גמליאל שתהא נודרת ליתומים כל מה שירצו כו' וקאמר רב הונא לא שנו אלא שלא ניסת אבל ניסת אין מדירין אותה דמיפר לה בעלה אפילו נדרה ברבים ואמאי אכתי נדיר אותה על דעת רבים שאין לו הפרה כדאמר אמימר הכא ויש לפרש דלענין נדרי אשתו אין לחלק בין ברבים בין על דעת רבים כיון דברבים יש לו הפרה לרב הונא ה"ה על דעת רבים בנדרי אשתו וכי פריך התם ארב הונא וליחוש דילמא אזלא לגבי חכם ושרי לה ומשני קסבר צריך לפרט את הנדר הוה מצי לשנויי דמדיר ליה על דעת רבים אלא דלא צריך ועוד י"ל דרב הונא לית ליה דאמימר דהא דקאמר אמימר אפילו למ"ד נדר שהודר ברבים כו' לאו אפלוגתא דאמוראי קאי דרב הונא ורב נחמן בריש השולח (שם) אלא אפלוגתא דר' יהודה ורבנן בסוף השולח (גיטין דף מו.):
notes.en: That we administer the vow on the consent of the public: one may ask from the beginning of the chapter HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 35b), about the widow, where Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel instituted that she vows to the orphans whatever they wish. Rav Huna says there: they taught this only when she has not remarried, but if she has remarried they do not administer the vow to her, since her husband can annul it for her even if she vowed in public. But why not? Let them still administer the vow on the consent of the public, which cannot be nullified, as Ameimar says here [on 46a]. One may explain that with regard to a wife’s vows there is no difference between “in public” and “on the consent of the public”: since according to Rav Huna her husband can annul a vow made in public, the same is true of one made on the consent of the public. And when [the Gemara] there challenges Rav Huna, “But let us be concerned that perhaps she will go to a Sage and he will release it,” and answers, “He holds that one must delineate the vow,” it could have answered that they administer it on the consent of the public, but it did not need to. Alternatively, Rav Huna does not hold like Ameimar: Ameimar’s statement, “even according to the one who says a vow taken in public…,” does not refer to the dispute of the Amoraim Rav Huna and Rav Naḥman at the beginning of HaSholeaḥ, but to the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis at the end of HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 46a).

messages.text: The answer continues on 46a: the vow is administered “on the consent of the public,” a kind of vow that cannot be dissolved without their consent.
